reference: Beasley, J.E., M. Krishnamoorthy, Y.M. Sharaiha and D. Abramson, 'Scheduling Aircraft Landings - The Static Case', Transportation Science, 34, 180-197, 2000.
math_formula:
### Mathematical Model
For aircraft set A:

Parameters:
- T_i: target landing time for aircraft i
- E_i, L_i: earliest and latest allowable landing time for aircraft i
- alpha_i, beta_i: early and late penalty per unit time
- s_{i,j}: required separation time if aircraft i lands before aircraft j
- M: big-M constant

Decision variables:
- x_i: actual landing time for aircraft i
- e_i, l_i: early and late deviation from target time
- y_{i,j} in {0,1}: 1 if aircraft i lands before aircraft j

$$
\begin{aligned}
&\text{Minimize} && \sum_{i \in A} (\alpha_i e_i + \beta_i l_i) \\
&\text{Subject to} && y_{i,j} + y_{j,i} = 1 && \forall i < j \\
& && x_j \geq x_i + s_{i,j} - M(1-y_{i,j}) && \forall i \neq j \\
& && E_i \leq x_i \leq L_i && \forall i \in A \\
& && e_i \geq T_i - x_i && \forall i \in A \\
& && l_i \geq x_i - T_i && \forall i \in A \\
& && e_i,l_i \geq 0,\quad y_{i,j}\in\{0,1\}.
\end{aligned}
$$
This is a static aircraft landing sequencing model. It does not assign aircraft types to routes, does not model passenger demand, and does not include fleet availability or route operating costs.
natural_language_example: An airport control team must schedule a bank of arriving aircraft. For each aircraft, the planners know its earliest allowable landing time, target landing time, latest allowable landing time, early-arrival penalty, and late-arrival penalty. For each ordered aircraft pair, safety rules specify the minimum separation time if one aircraft lands before the other. The decision is the actual landing time of each aircraft and the pairwise landing order. The objective is to minimize total early and late landing penalties while satisfying landing windows and separation requirements. This is not an aircraft fleet assignment or route allocation problem.
